657Propose h9Reconsider whether correlated normal power-delivery and ambient errors plus one or more sensor gain faults explain the observations without a thermal model fault; repeated rejected global-boundary conclusions require checking this rival explicitly.
658NoteNormal delivery tolerance ±4% and sensor slopes ±3% can shift the apparent cooling ratio materially. Thus least-squares R ratio ~1.15 is not a direct estimate of physical ratio: R ratio up to ~1.20 remains feasible with ordinary negative delivery/slopes. A cooling ratio 1.20 implies core0 true gain near .88 after allowance for normal slope. Need compare joint nuisance fit rather than keep treating their means as known zero.
659Propose h10Global boundary conductance may be overstated by about +20% rather than +15%, while core0 gain error is about −12%; normal negative delivery and slope errors can bias the naive thermal estimate downward.
